test_title: RRB NTPC CBT-I Official Paper (Held On: 22 Feb 2021 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: A box contains 6 white balls and 7 black balls. Two balls are drawn at random. What is the probability that both of them are of different colours?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Required probability = (Ways to choose 1 White × Ways to choose 1 Black) ÷ Total ways to choose 2 balls

Probability = (6 × 7) ÷ ¹³C₂

Probability = 42 ÷ [(13 × 12) ÷ 2]

Probability = 42 ÷ 78 = 7 / 13

**∴ The correct answer is 7 / 13.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Number of white balls = 6

Number of black balls = 7

Total number of balls = 6 + 7 = 13

 
 
 6 White Balls
 7 Black Balls
 

 Total = 13 Balls
 Draw 2 Balls → 1 White & 1 Black → 42 ways

**Formula Used:**

Probability = Favorable Outcomes ÷ Total Possible Outcomes

ⁿCᵣ = n! ÷ [r! × (n − r)!]

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total possible outcomes of drawing 2 balls from 13 = ¹³C₂

⇒ ¹³C₂ = (13 × 12) ÷ (2 × 1) = 78

⇒ For the balls to be of different colours, 1 white ball and 1 black ball must be drawn.

⇒ Favorable outcomes = ⁶C₁ × ⁷C₁

⇒ Favorable outcomes = 6 × 7 = 42

⇒ Required Probability = 42 ÷ 78

⇒ Dividing numerator and denominator by 6, we get 7 / 13

**∴ The correct answer is 7 / 13.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Combination vs Permutation

Combination (ⁿCᵣ) is used when the order of selection does not matter. Permutation (ⁿPᵣ) is used when arrangement or sequence order is important.

Independent Events

Two events are independent if the occurrence of one does not affect the probability of the other. For independent events A and B: P(A and B) = P(A) × P(B).

Mutually Exclusive Events

Events that cannot occur simultaneously at the exact same time. For mutually exclusive events A and B: P(A or B) = P(A) + P(B).
